CRT Display Devices
Structure of CRT Display Devices
Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) with Deflection Elements

Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) with Deflection Elements
Figure source: web

Electron Gun
❖ Components of the Electron Gun
• The heated metal cathode
• A control grid
❖ Heat is supplied to the cathode by directing a current through a coil of 
wire (the filament) inside the cathode.
❖ This causes electrons to be “boiled off” the hot cathode surface.
❖ Then, the free, negatively electrons are then accelerated towards the 
phosphor coating by a high positive voltage.
❖ Phosphor is a substance which when absorbs a photon (some form of 
energy) it emits a photon of longer wavelength.

Intensity Control
❖ Intensity of the electron beam is controlled by the voltage at the control 
grid.
❖ A high negative voltage applied to the control grid will shut off the beam.
❖ A smaller negative voltage on the control grid increases the number of 
electrons passing through.
❖ The brightness of a display point is controlled by varying the voltage 
on the control grid.

Cathode-Ray Tubes (CRT)
❖A beam of electrons emitted by an electron gun, passes 
through focusing and deflection systems that direct the 
beam toward specified positions on the phosphor-coated 
screen.
❖Because the light emitted by the phosphor fades very rabidly, the 
refresh process is needed to maintain the picture on the screen.

Deflection and Emission of Light
❖The focusing system forces the electron beam to converge to a small cross 
section as it strikes the phosphor.
❖Deflection of the electron beam can be controlled by the deflection coils.
❖Spots of light is produced on the screen by the transfer of the CRT beam 
energy to the phosphor.
❖Electron in the beam collide with the phosphor coating, they stopped and 
their kinetic energy is absorbed by the phosphor. 
❖ Total beam energy = heat energy (due to friction) + reminder causes 
electrons in the phosphor atoms to move up to higher quantum-energy 
levels.
❖ After short time, the excited electrons fall back to their stable ground state, 
releasing up extra energy as small quantum of light energy.

❖Persistence: how long phosphors continue to emit light after the CRT 
beam is removed.
❖Persistence is defined as the time that the emitted light takes from the 
screen to decay to one-tenth of its original intensity.
❖Lower-persistence phosphors require high refresh rates to maintain a 
picture definition on the screen without flicker, and it is very much 
useful for animation.
❖Higher-persistence phosphors  are useful for displaying highly complex, 
static pictures. 
Persistence & Refresh Rate

Types of Graphics Display Devices 
❖Based on the way pixels excited on the screen, display devices is of two 
types:
❖ Vector Scan (also know as random scan or calligraphic devices) :  
a set of dedicated pixels along a line or a curve is excited.
❖ Raster Scan : all the pixels on a screen are excited regardless the 
type of objects that it needs to display..

Random Scan Display System 
❖Also called Vector, Stroke, Line drawing displays.
❖Characters are also made of sequences of strokes (or short lines)
❖Vectored – electron beam is deflected from end-point to end-point.
❖Random scan – Order of deflection is dictated by the arbitrary order of 
the display commands.
❖ Phosphor has short persistence i.e., 10-100 micro-second, hence display 
must be refreshed at regular interval (>30Hz).

Random-Scan Display System
❖Advantages: 
• A CRT has the electron beam directed only to the parts of the screen where 
the graphics is to be drawn.
• Produce smooth line drawings.
• Refresh rate depends upon the no. of line to be drawn
❖ Disadvantage: 
• Random-Scan monitors cannot display realistic shades scenes.
• It is costly as it required high precision devices. 
• Used in gaming devices such Asteroids video games and Tempest 
video game
